title: Construction of constructible truncations
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum
$p,a,q,k_0,k$, where $q=p^a$. Fix a prime $\ell\neq p$, write
$\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$, choose an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\Ql$, and
choose a finite extension $E/\Ql$ contained in $\Qlb$. Let $Y$ be a
finite-type $k$-scheme, where
finite type is the scheme
condition used throughout. Let
$\Lambda\in\{E,\Qlb\}$. For $\Lambda=E$, let
$D^b_c(Y,E)$ be the
rationalized
category obtained
from integral complexes whose finite-level reductions satisfy the
finite-torsion
constructibility condition; for $\Lambda=\Qlb$, use the
common finite-stage
coefficient construction. The symbols $\mathcal H^r$ denote the
cohomology sheaves of a
derived complex. Let $m,i\in\mathbf Z$.
There are truncation functors

$$
\tau^{\leq m},\tau^{\geq m}:D^b_c(Y,\Lambda)
\longrightarrow D^b_c(Y,\Lambda).
$$

At a common finite coefficient field they are the
standard truncations of the
constructible derived category; they commute with finite scalar extension and
with the transitions of the coefficient tower.
For $\Lambda=E$ or $\Qlb$, these truncations, their natural maps, and the
distinguished truncation triangles satisfy the axioms of a
bounded t-structure. For
$K\in D^b_c(Y,\Lambda)$, define its cohomology functors by

$$
\mathcal H^i(K)=\bigl(\tau^{\geq i}\tau^{\leq i}K\bigr)[i].
$$

For every scheme automorphism $h:Y\xrightarrow{\sim}Y$, the
derived pullback $Lh^*$
commutes with the truncations and with $\mathcal H^i$.

note: *Recorded in advance* from chapter *Verification of the operations and cohomological interfaces* of the source.

proof.text: Write $A=\mathcal O_E$, $R=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}$, and $\mathcal C_A=D^b_c(Y,A)$. The scheme $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is noetherian and quasi-compact: a field has just the ideals $(0)$ and $(1)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] to $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. Apply [lem-fin-finite-type-fibre-dimension-bound] to the same morphism; its only fibre is $Y$, so $Y$ is finite-dimensional. Finally $\ell$ is a unit in $k$ because $\ell\ne p$, and its image is a unit in each local ring of $Y$. All hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization] now hold. Its explicit comparison clause identifies the full subcategory of [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed] with the completed bounded constructible category used by the integral and localized t-structure theorems, with the same ring sheaf and reduction functors. In particular the compatible etale-origin witnesses and uniform local models required there are supplied by this cited theorem; they are not inferred merely from the notation $D^b_c$.

source.place: Proof, integral-category passage; geometric hypotheses and identification of integral conventions

proof.text: At a torsion coefficient level, use the standard t-structure of [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category]. Canonical upper truncation replaces the cutoff term by a kernel and canonical lower truncation replaces its cutoff term by a cokernel, as in Stacks Tag 0118 (homology-section-truncations). Their surviving cohomology sheaves are exactly the original ones and the other cohomology sheaves are zero; the upper calculation is [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-cohomology], and the lower calculation follows directly by taking $\operatorname{coker}d^{m-1}$ in degree $m$. Thus boundedness and the finite partitions in [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility] survive truncation. The standard triangles restrict to this full triangulated subcategory. At the integral stage, apply [prop-weil-pbc-integral-tstructure] after step 1: it supplies the bounded t-structure, both ambient canonical truncation restrictions, their maps and their distinguished triangles on all of $\mathcal C_A$. This application uses no flat-cohomology assumption. It also does not identify the reductions of an arbitrary integral truncation with the truncations of the reductions; such an identification has the extra Tor hypothesis recorded in the cited integral theorem.

source.place: Proof, first four sentences: finite and integral truncations; corrected use of ambient integral truncations

proof.text: Use the raw scalar localization of [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], so that $\mathcal C_E=\mathcal C_A[1/\varpi_E]$ has the same objects and localized Hom groups; no idempotent completion is involved. By step 1 the categories and localization functor are exactly those in [prop-weil-localized-tstructure]. That theorem gives the bounded t-structure on $\mathcal C_E$, its natural truncation comparisons $\tau_E^{\le m}QK\cong Q\tau_A^{\le m}K$ and $\tau_E^{\ge m}QK\cong Q\tau_A^{\ge m}K$, and t-exactness of $Q$. Apply [lem-pod-texact-truncation-comparison] to the t-exact exact functor $Q$: its characterizing equations identify the canonical truncation maps with the localized integral maps under these comparisons. The resulting truncation triangle is the image of the integral one, since $Q$ is exact and its two end objects lie in the required halves. This identifies the finite coefficient-field t-structure with the rational standard pair of [def-weil-constructible-standard-tstructure].

Let $E\subset L$ be finite coefficient fields, and put $S=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{L,Y}$. By [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison], $S$ is finite free over $R$ and, for a derived-complete $K$, the actual integral scalar extension is naturally $K\otimes_R^L S$. Choose an $R$-basis of $S$ solely to check exactness: after forgetting the $S$-action, tensoring any module sheaf with $S$ is a finite direct sum of copies of that module sheaf. Finite direct sums preserve kernels and cokernels, so this tensor functor is exact. Apply [lem-sp-exact-functor-preserves-homology] to obtain $\mathcal H^r(K\otimes_R^L S)\cong\mathcal H^r(K)\otimes_R S$ naturally. It preserves both cohomological half-categories, and [lem-weil-integral-scalar-extension-constructible] supplies membership in the target integral category. Hence integral scalar extension is t-exact; after localization the same is true of $-\otimes_E L$, since the rational halves are the isomorphism closures of integral halves. This rational functor is triangulated by [lem-weil-scalar-extension-exact-triangulated]. Apply [lem-pod-texact-truncation-comparison] to this t-exact triangulated functor to obtain the two natural truncation isomorphisms, compatible with their canonical maps. Its identity, composition and natural-transformation clauses apply to the canonical scalar associators of [lem-weil-scalar-extension-composition]. The unit and pentagon equations for these associators are explicitly supplied by [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension]; the comparison lemma preserves those equations, giving coherence over the coefficient-field tower. These are finite field extensions, not non-flat reductions $A/\varpi^{n+1}\to A/\varpi^n$.

source.place: Proof, scalar-extension and coefficient-tower compatibility; exactness and t-exactness supplied explicitly

proof.text: Apply [lem-sbc-coherent-pair-functor-descent] to the additive finite-stage categories and the upper truncation functors, with the coherent scalar comparisons supplied by step 4. The pair category is exactly [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. It gives $\tau^{\le m}(E,K)=(E,\tau_E^{\le m}K)$; an arrow represented by $u$ over $L$ is sent to $\tau_L^{\le m}(u)$ conjugated by the step-4 scalar comparisons. The cited lemma proves independence of the representative and common field, and preservation of identities and composition. Apply it again to lower truncation. The step-4 comparisons preserve the canonical truncation maps, so these maps are compatible transformations and descend by the same lemma. The finite-stage truncation triangles then give triangles in the pair category, distinguished by its stated common-stage convention. This constructs the truncations, maps and triangles with every common finite-field presentation.

source.place: Proof, descent of truncation functors and triangles to the common-stage category

proof.text: For $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, take the two standard classes of [def-weil-constructible-standard-tstructure], namely objects isomorphic to finite-stage nonpositive or nonnegative objects. Shifting such a representative proves the two shift inclusions in [def-weil-t-structure]. For orthogonality, replace the source and target by representatives in degrees $\le0$ and $\ge1$, and extend both to one common field. By step 4 these bounds persist under every further field extension. The finite-stage Hom group is therefore zero at every such stage, and its directed colimit, the Hom group of [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], is zero. The triangle constructed in step 5 has its end terms in the required halves, giving the truncation axiom. Finally an object $(E,K)$ has upper and lower bounds already over $E$ by step 3; the same bounds work in the common-stage category. This proves all t-structure axioms and boundedness, rather than assuming that functorial descent alone proves them.

source.place: Proof, bounded t-structure at algebraically closed coefficients

proof.text: For either field stage define $\mathcal H^i$ to be the composite $K\mapsto(\tau^{\ge i}\tau^{\le i}K)[i]$ displayed in the statement. The truncation maps are functorial, so this is a functor. Its value lies in the heart: before shifting it has only degree $i$, and the cohomological shift $[i]$ moves that degree to zero. At the integral and torsion stages it is the degree-$i$ cohomology sheaf of [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves], placed in degree zero, by the kernel/image descriptions; at a field stage it is its rationalized or common-stage heart object. Thus no identification of an abstract rational heart with an ambient category of $E$-sheaves is assumed.

source.place: Proof, displayed definition of cohomology functors

proof.text: Let $h:Y\xrightarrow{\sim}Y$ be a scheme automorphism. By [lem-weil-isomorphism-derived-pullback], with the completed integral coefficient sheaf, the actual integral pullback of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] is naturally isomorphic to termwise $h^{-1}$ on every object of $\mathcal C_A$, and its values remain in $\mathcal C_A$. This is the entire completed-derived-to-termwise comparison; no cone or K-flat argument is needed here. By [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image], $h^{-1}$ is an exact equivalence of sheaves, with the compatible coefficient identifications. After transporting the module action along the completed coefficient isomorphism, it is also an exact equivalence on module sheaves. By [lem-sp-exact-functor-preserves-homology], $\mathcal H^r(h^{-1}K)\cong h^{-1}\mathcal H^r(K)$, so it preserves both integral half-categories. The termwise derived functor is triangulated by [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated]. Use its shift structure on the naturally identified integral pullback. After step 1's identification of integral conventions, [prop-weil-pbc-rational-transport] makes its coefficient-linear rational extension triangulated. Its pure-tensor action is the prescribed action in [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], so it is the actual $Lh_E^*$. The rational halves are isomorphism closures of integral halves, hence this functor is t-exact too. Apply [lem-pod-texact-truncation-comparison] to obtain the natural isomorphisms $\alpha_{E,m}^{\pm}:Lh_E^*\tau_E^{\le m,\ge m}\cong\tau_E^{\le m,\ge m}Lh_E^*$, preserving the canonical maps.

source.place: Proof, automorphism compatibility; exact module equivalence and t-exactness replace the invalid triangulated-exactness inference

proof.text: Write $F_E=Lh_E^*$ and $T_{L/E}=-\otimes_E L$. The first comparison of [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension] applied to $h$ gives an integral natural isomorphism between the integral versions of $T_{L/E}F_E$ and $F_LT_{L/E}$, with identity and tower equations. Its hypotheses hold by step 1 and the constructible membership in step 8. Apply [lem-pur-semilinear-scalar-localization] with $R=\mathcal O_E$, $S=\mathcal O_L$, $t=\varpi_E$, $u=\varpi_L$, and the inclusion $R\to S$. The two integral composite functors are semilinear for this inclusion, since scalar extension transports the module action and inverse image preserves it. The image of $\varpi_E$ is nonzero in the field $L=S[1/\varpi_L]$, hence invertible. The lemma extends the integral comparison to $\beta_{L/E}:T_{L/E}F_E\xrightarrow{\sim}F_LT_{L/E}$ on all rational morphisms and preserves its identity and tower equations, including whiskering across different valuation rings. Its fraction formula agrees with the pure-tensor rules of [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] and [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], so these extensions are the actual rational composite functors.

source.place: Proof, final automorphism sentence: rational descent of the scalar/pullback comparison

proof.text:
Fix either truncation $\tau$ and its cutoff. Write $T=T_{L/E}$ and $c_K:T\tau_EK\xrightarrow{\sim}\tau_LTK$ for the scalar comparison of step 4. Step 8 gives $\alpha_E:F_E\tau_E\xrightarrow{\sim}\tau_EF_E$. All $T,F_E$ are t-exact triangulated functors. Apply the natural-transformation clause of [lem-pod-texact-truncation-comparison] to $\beta:TF_E\Rightarrow F_LT$ from step 9, and its composition clause to both composites. At every $K$ this gives
$$
 \alpha_{L,TK}\circ F_L(c_K)\circ\beta_{\tau_EK}
 =\tau_L(\beta_K)\circ c_{F_EK}\circ T(\alpha_{E,K}).
$$
Both sides map $TF_E\tau_EK$ to $\tau_LF_LTK$. For the families $\Phi_E=F_E\tau_E$ and $\Psi_E=\tau_EF_E$, their scalar comparisons are respectively $b_K=F_L(c_K)\circ\beta_{\tau_EK}$ and $d_K=\tau_L(\beta_K)\circ c_{F_EK}$. Thus the displayed equation is precisely $\alpha_LT\circ b=d\circ T\alpha_E$, the transformation hypothesis of [lem-sbc-coherent-pair-functor-descent]. The unit and tower hypotheses for $b,d$ follow from steps 4 and 9 and the lemma's composition clause. Descent sends $\alpha$ and its inverse to mutually inverse transformations. Its composition clause identifies the descended families with the composites of the actual common-stage pullback of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] and the truncation of step 5: their representative formulas use exactly $\beta$ and $c$. This proves both truncation comparisons over $\Qlb$.

source.place: Proof, final automorphism sentence: common-stage descent of the compatible truncation comparisons

proof.text:
The integral and rational pullback functors commute with shifts by the triangulated structures established in step 8. For the algebraically closed stage use the final particular assertion of [prop-weil-pbc-descent-functors]: the scalar-compatible family $(Lg_E^*)_E$ descends to an exact functor. Its representative formula is precisely the pullback formula of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]; step 1 identifies its integral and rational conventions, and [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients] identifies the same pair category. Thus this assertion supplies shift compatibility for the actual common-stage pullback, without asserting it for arbitrary natural comparisons. Compose the shift comparison with the two truncation comparisons of steps 8 and 10, at cutoff $i$. For $\Lambda=E$ or $\Qlb$ this gives
$$
 Lh^*((\tau^{\ge i}\tau^{\le i}K)[i])\cong(\tau^{\ge i}Lh^*\tau^{\le i}K)[i]\cong(\tau^{\ge i}\tau^{\le i}Lh^*K)[i].
$$
By step 7 this is the required natural isomorphism $Lh^*\mathcal H^i(K)\cong\mathcal H^i(Lh^*K)$.
